guide.summary: Imperial palaces, parks, national museums and contemporary art, with duck restaurants, hotel dining, breakfast, a cocktail bar, a patisserie and a hutong café checked against their own or their public operators' websites.
guide.tip: Book the Palace Museum ahead (reservations open up to seven days before at 20:00) and avoid Mondays, when it, the National Museum of China and the National Art Museum of China are closed; the Capital Museum and Beijing Planetarium close on Tuesdays instead.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: The Palace Museum, National Museum of China, National Art Museum of China, Prince Gong Mansion and China Science and Technology Museum close on Mondays except public holidays. The Capital Museum, Beijing Planetarium and Beijing Ancient Observatory close on Tuesdays instead.

toolkit.label: Booking
toolkit.copy: Palace Museum reservations open up to 7 days ahead from 20:00 and entry is by ID scan. The National Museum of China is free but needs a real-name booking, limited to one booking a week for up to five people per account.

toolkit.label: Entry and queues
toolkit.copy: At the Palace Museum you can only enter through the Meridian Gate (Wumen, south) and leave by the Shenwu or Donghua gates. At the National Museum of China you queue at the north gate during your booked slot with the original ID used to book.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: UCCA Beijing bars food, drinks, tripods, selfie sticks, suitcases and bags longer than 40 cm from galleries, offers free lockers, and admits children under 1.2 m free with an adult. Country Kitchen, The House of Dynasties and Mei at Rosewood Beijing ask for business casual.

guide.dek: Book the big museums a week out, plan around Monday and Tuesday closures, and keep the hutong cafés and hotel dining rooms for the gaps.
intro: Start with the Palace Museum, where you must book ahead: reservations open up to seven days before your visit at 20:00, and entry is by scanning your ID. You go in only through the Meridian Gate on the south side and leave by the Shenwu or Donghua gates. Admission runs from 08:30 to a last entry at 16:00, and the palace is closed on Mondays except public holidays. Some halls are shut, including Yanxi Palace, and the Wuyingdian has stopped opening.

The National Museum of China, on the east side of Tiananmen Square at 16 East Chang'an Avenue, is free but needs a real-name booking, and accounts are limited to one booking a week for up to five people. Its painting and calligraphy exhibition on poetic dwelling opened on 4 September 2026 in South Hall 12. Nearby, the National Art Museum of China shows Nikolai Fechin paintings until 14 February 2027. At Prince Gong Mansion, a centenary exhibition on Pu Xinyu and Zhang Daqian runs until 13 December.

For contemporary art, UCCA Beijing in the 798 district has Carsten Höller: Two until 31 January 2027 and opens Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00 to 19:00. With children, you can head to the China Science and Technology Museum, where tickets open seven days ahead at 18:00. The Beijing Planetarium and the Ancient Observatory share 09:00 to 16:30 hours and close on Tuesdays. For an evening, the National Centre for the Performing Arts lists Tosca from 6 to 8 November.

For food, Quanjude's Qianmen branch is at 30 Qianmen Street and Bianyifang has a branch on Xianyukou Street. Donglaishun serves at 198 Wangfujing Street. At Rosewood Beijing, LIQĀ serves breakfast from 6:30. Country Kitchen and The House of Dynasties serve lunch and dinner daily, and Mei pours cocktails from 7 pm. In the Gulou area, Café Zarah serves north European breakfast and closes on Mondays. Toast at The Orchid is open to non-guests from 10:00 to 21:30.
summaryCards: Book the Palace Museum up to seven days ahead, enter by the Meridian Gate, and pair it with the free, pre-booked National Museum of China on any day but Monday.
Start with breakfast at LIQĀ or Café Zarah, then walk in Beihai Park or visit Prince Gong Mansion, which opens at 8:30.
Bring the original ID you booked with, since the Palace Museum and National Museum of China check it at entry, and note that the Capital Museum and Planetarium close on Tuesdays.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. The Temple of Heaven, Summer Palace, Beihai Park and Beijing Zoo were confirmed through the Beijing Municipal Administration Center of Parks, which gives management-office addresses and recent 2026 activity notices but not public opening hours; their own sites could not be read (connection refused or certificate errors). The Palace Museum publishes its entrance gate but no street address on the pages read, and its English site returned HTTP 502. Mutianyu Great Wall and the National Stadium are clearly operating but published no address on the pages read, so they are not used. Restaurant hours were not published for Quanjude, Bianyifang or Donglaishun, and their operating evidence is group-level 2026 content. Universal Beijing Resort's park schedule page returned no readable hours. Butterfly Patisserie's only dated marker is a 2026 page footer. Several hotel and café sites (Peninsula, Bulgari, Four Seasons, Park Hyatt, Shangri-La, Lama Temple, % Arabica) blocked automated reading, and TRB Hutong and Da Dong had certificate errors, so there are few confirmed coffee, bakery and cocktail options. Capital Museum's hours are described as provisional ("暂定").
